title: Equality of two split searches
statement: For all $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$, the partial functions on natural numbers given by the least $i\le m$ satisfying $i+(C+1)(i+1)^c=m$, when such an $i$ exists, and undefined otherwise, are equal.
replaced:
For $D, e, m \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\mathrm{solve}_{D,e}(m)$ be the least $i \le m$
with $i + D(i+1)^e = m$, undefined if there is none, and for $C, c, m \in \mathbb{N}$
let $\mathrm{split}_{C,c}(m)$ be the least $n \le m$ with
$n + (C+1)(n+1)^c = m$, undefined if there is none. Then for all
$C, c \in \mathbb{N}$, the partial functions $\mathrm{solve}_{C+1,c}$ and
$\mathrm{split}_{C,c}$ on $\mathbb{N}$ are equal.
